sanskrit_verse:
आढ्यस्य निकटस्थस्य यच् छक्तेन न याचितम् ।
शुद्धर्णाशङ्कया तत्र लेख्यं दुर्बलतां यात् ॥
transliteration: āḍhyasya nikātasthasya yac chaktena na yācitam | śuddharṇāśaṅkayā tatra lekhyaṃ durbalatām iyāt ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When a capable person near the affluent fails to request what is rightfully theirs through pure intent and without suspicion, the written record shall declare their state as weakened.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from capacity, not proximity alone
Causation lies in conscious omission, not external compulsion
Capacity-based responsibility requires active assertion of right
Restoration logic demands recognition of unclaimed integrity
Consciousness alignment occurs when claim aligns with purity of intent
executable_legal_axioms: IF (proximity_to_affluent = true AND capability = verified AND request_made = false AND intent_purity = confirmed) THEN (status = weakened)
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, this axiom establishes that mere association or access does not confer enforceable entitlement; only conscious invocation rooted in pure intent activates legitimate claim. Courts must assess both factual position and ontological clarity of the actor's will.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that absence of request despite ability constitutes causal error, not moral failure. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential weakening due to disuse of rightful standing. Responsibility remains proportional to realized awareness. No punitive inference arises—only restoration of dormant capacity.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process for unexpressed claims
Realign consciousness through affirmation of inherent worthiness
Restore capacity by removing internalized limitation patterns
Facilitate reintegration via acknowledgment of original entitlement
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. Justice flows from consciousness realignment, not punitive design. Reality responds to authentic claim. Dharma is restored.
